================================================================================
   DAILY GIT WORKFLOW
================================================================================

1️⃣  CHECK STATUS (See what's changed)
   git status

2️⃣  VIEW CHANGES (See what you modified)
   git diff

3️⃣  ADD CHANGES (Stage files for commit)
   # Add specific file
   git add app.py
   
   # Add all modified files
   git add -u
   
   # Add everything (be careful!)
   git add .

4️⃣  COMMIT CHANGES (Save to repository)
   git commit -m "Description of what you changed"

5️⃣  VIEW HISTORY (See past commits)
   git log --oneline
   git log --graph --oneline --all

================================================================================
   COMMON GIT COMMANDS
================================================================================

📊 VIEWING STATUS & HISTORY:
   git status              # Check current status
   git log                 # View commit history
   git log --oneline       # Compact history view
   git diff                # See uncommitted changes
   git diff HEAD~1         # Compare with previous commit
   git show <commit-id>    # View specific commit details

📝 MAKING CHANGES:
   git add <file>          # Stage a file
   git add -u              # Stage all modified files
   git commit -m "msg"     # Commit with message
   git commit -am "msg"    # Add all & commit (modified files only)

↩️  UNDOING CHANGES:
   git checkout -- <file>  # Discard changes to file
   git reset HEAD <file>   # Unstage a file
   git reset --soft HEAD~1 # Undo last commit (keep changes)
   git reset --hard HEAD~1 # Undo last commit (discard changes)

🌳 BRANCHING:
   git branch              # List branches
   git branch <name>       # Create new branch
   git checkout <name>     # Switch to branch
   git checkout -b <name>  # Create and switch to branch
   git merge <branch>      # Merge branch into current

🏷️  TAGGING (For releases):
   git tag v1.0.0          # Create lightweight tag
   git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Release version 1.0.0"  # Annotated tag
   git tag                 # List all tags

================================================================================
   EXAMPLE WORKFLOWS
================================================================================

📌 SCENARIO 1: Made changes to app.py and want to commit
   git status
   git diff app.py                  # Review changes
   git add app.py
   git commit -m "Fixed SSH connection timeout issue"

📌 SCENARIO 2: Modified multiple files
   git status
   git add app.py controllers/device_controller.py
   git commit -m "Updated device controller and main app"

📌 SCENARIO 3: Want to see what changed in last 5 commits
   git log --oneline -5
   git show <commit-id>             # View specific commit

📌 SCENARIO 4: Made a mistake, want to undo
   git status
   git checkout -- app.py           # Discard changes to app.py
   # OR
   git reset --hard HEAD            # Discard ALL changes

📌 SCENARIO 5: Create a new feature branch
   git checkout -b feature-email-notifications
   # Make changes...
   git add <files>
   git commit -m "Added email notifications"
   git checkout main                # Switch back to main
   git merge feature-email-notifications  # Merge feature

📌 SCENARIO 6: Tag a release version
   git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "First production release"
   git tag                          # View all tags

   SETTING UP REMOTE REPOSITORY (GITHUB/GITLAB)
================================================================================

To make this accessible only to you on GitHub (PRIVATE):

1️⃣  CREATE PRIVATE GITHUB REPO:
   - Go to https://github.com/new
   - Name: RDK-Device-Manager
   - Description: Flask-based RDK device testing platform
   - ✅ Select "Private" (IMPORTANT!)
   - Don't initialize with README
   - Click "Create repository"

2️⃣  LINK YOUR LOCAL REPO TO GITHUB:
   git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/RDK-Device-Manager.git
   git push -u origin main

3️⃣  FUTURE PUSHES:
   git push                         # Push to GitHub

4️⃣  CLONE ON NEW MACHINE:
   git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/RDK-Device-Manager.git
   cd RDK-Device-Manager
   ./install_complete_system.sh

ALTERNATIVE: GitLab (More private-friendly):
   - Go to https://gitlab.com
   - Create new private project
   - Follow similar steps as above

================================================================================
   USING GIT WITH NEW RASPBERRY PI
================================================================================

When setting up on a new Raspberry Pi:

1️⃣  INSTALL GIT:
   sudo apt install git

2️⃣  CONFIGURE GIT:
   git config --global user.name "Your Name"
   git config --global user.email "your.email@example.com"

3️⃣  CLONE REPOSITORY (if using GitHub/GitLab):
   git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/RDK-Device-Manager.git
   cd RDK-Device-Manager

4️⃣  RUN INSTALLATION:
   ./install_complete_system.sh

5️⃣  COPY SENSITIVE DATA (manually):
   # Copy from backup:
   cp /path/to/backup/devices.json ./
   cp /path/to/backup/users.json ./

================================================================================
   BEST PRACTICES
================================================================================

✅ DO:
   - Commit frequently with clear messages
   - Use branches for new features
   - Review changes before committing (git diff)
   - Write descriptive commit messages
   - Tag release versions
   - Keep sensitive data out of Git (.gitignore)
   - Back up devices.json and users.json separately

❌ DON'T:
   - Commit devices.json or users.json
   - Commit passwords or API keys
   - Make huge commits (commit incrementally)
   - Use vague commit messages like "fixed stuff"
   - Commit generated files (logs, screenshots, __pycache__)
   - Force push to main branch

================================================================================
   COMMIT MESSAGE CONVENTIONS
================================================================================

Good commit message format:

   [Type]: Brief description (50 chars or less)
   
   Optional longer explanation of what and why.

Types:
   feat:     New feature
   fix:      Bug fix
   docs:     Documentation changes
   refactor: Code restructuring (no behavior change)
   test:     Adding tests
   chore:    Maintenance tasks
   perf:     Performance improvements

Examples:
   feat: Add email notification support for test failures
   fix: Resolve SSH timeout issue with slow devices
   docs: Update installation guide with new requirements
   refactor: Extract queue logic to separate service
   chore: Update dependencies to latest versions

================================================================================
   CHECKING WHAT'S IN GIT VS WHAT'S NOT
================================================================================

View all tracked files:
   git ls-files

View all ignored files:
   git status --ignored

View what's being ignored by .gitignore:
   git check-ignore -v <filename>

See what would be added:
   git add --dry-run .
